report:
**Conclusion: Supported.** The adjuvanted recombinant zoster vaccine (RZV; Shingrix) substantially reduces herpes zoster (shingles) in adults aged 70 years or older.

The pivotal randomized, placebo-controlled ZOE-70 trial found vaccine efficacy of **89.8%** (95% CI, 84.2%–93.7%) against shingles in adults ≥70. Protection was similar for ages 70–79 (90.0%) and ≥80 (89.1%). This is direct high-quality evidence for the claim.

CDC summarizes pooled trial evidence as **91.3% efficacy** against shingles after more than three years among adults ≥70, consistent with sustained high protection. The trial enrolled roughly 13,900 adults ≥70 and compared two vaccine doses with placebo.

These results apply chiefly to the studied two-dose regimen in immunocompetent older adults; efficacy is not the same as a guarantee that no vaccinated person will develop shingles.

Sources:  
- https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27626517/  
- https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa1603800  
- https://www.cdc.gov/pinkbook/hcp/table-of-contents/chapter-23-zoster.html  
- https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT01165229
